CreateCentralizationRuleForOrganization.name: CreateCentralizationRuleForOrganization
CreateCentralizationRuleForOrganization.documentation: Creates a centralization rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

CreateConnector.name: CreateConnector
CreateConnector.documentation: Creates a connector to a third-party cloud provider. With a connector, you can discover resources in the provider and collect their telemetry. Currently, Microsoft Azure is the only supported provider.

CreateDatasetIntegration.name: CreateDatasetIntegration
CreateDatasetIntegration.documentation:
Creates a dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region and returns its ARN.

To use this operation, you must have permission to access the dataset integration resources through the IAM role specified in the RoleArn parameter.

If a dataset integration already exists for the account, this operation fails with a ConflictException.

CreateS3TableIntegration.name: CreateS3TableIntegration
CreateS3TableIntegration.documentation: Creates an integration between CloudWatch and S3 Tables for analytics. This integration enables querying CloudWatch telemetry data using analytics engines like Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, and Apache Spark.

CreateTelemetryPipeline.name: CreateTelemetryPipeline
CreateTelemetryPipeline.documentation: Creates a telemetry pipeline for processing and transforming telemetry data. The pipeline defines how data flows from sources through processors to destinations, enabling data transformation and delivering capabilities.

CreateTelemetryRule.name: CreateTelemetryRule
CreateTelemetryRule.documentation: Creates a telemetry rule that defines how telemetry should be configured for Amazon Web Services resources in your account. The rule specifies which resources should have telemetry enabled and how that telemetry data should be collected based on resource type, telemetry type, and selection criteria.

CreateTelemetryRuleForOrganization.name: CreateTelemetryRuleForOrganization
CreateTelemetryRuleForOrganization.documentation: Creates a telemetry rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

DeleteCentralizationRuleForOrganization.name: DeleteCentralizationRuleForOrganization
DeleteCentralizationRuleForOrganization.documentation: Deletes an organization-wide centralization rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

DeleteConnector.name: DeleteConnector
DeleteConnector.documentation: Deletes a connector and its telemetry manifest.

DeleteDatasetIntegration.name: DeleteDatasetIntegration
DeleteDatasetIntegration.documentation: Deletes a dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region. This operation is idempotent; if you submit the same delete more than once, each call succeeds.

DeleteS3TableIntegration.name: DeleteS3TableIntegration
DeleteS3TableIntegration.documentation: Deletes an S3 Table integration and its associated data. This operation removes the connection between CloudWatch Observability Admin and S3 Tables.

DeleteTelemetryPipeline.name: DeleteTelemetryPipeline
DeleteTelemetryPipeline.documentation: Deletes a telemetry pipeline and its associated resources. This operation stops data processing and removes the pipeline configuration.

DeleteTelemetryRule.name: DeleteTelemetryRule
DeleteTelemetryRule.documentation: Deletes a telemetry rule from your account. Any telemetry configurations previously created by the rule will remain but no new resources will be configured by this rule.

DeleteTelemetryRuleForOrganization.name: DeleteTelemetryRuleForOrganization
DeleteTelemetryRuleForOrganization.documentation: Deletes an organization-wide telemetry rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

GetCentralizationRuleForOrganization.name: GetCentralizationRuleForOrganization
GetCentralizationRuleForOrganization.documentation: Retrieves the details of a specific organization centralization rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

GetConnectorTelemetryManifest.name: GetConnectorTelemetryManifest
GetConnectorTelemetryManifest.documentation: Retrieves the telemetry manifest of a connector and its current version. If the connector has no telemetry manifest, this operation returns a ResourceNotFoundException.

GetConnectorTelemetrySetup.name: GetConnectorTelemetrySetup
GetConnectorTelemetrySetup.documentation: Generates the artifacts that you use to create the infrastructure in your cloud provider that delivers the telemetry declared in the connector's telemetry manifest. This operation doesn't change any resources in your cloud provider or in Amazon Web Services.

GetDatasetIntegration.name: GetDatasetIntegration
GetDatasetIntegration.documentation: Returns the dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region.

GetS3TableIntegration.name: GetS3TableIntegration
GetS3TableIntegration.documentation: Retrieves information about a specific S3 Table integration, including its configuration, status, and metadata.

GetTelemetryEnrichmentStatus.name: GetTelemetryEnrichmentStatus
GetTelemetryEnrichmentStatus.documentation: Returns the current status of the resource tags for telemetry feature, which enhances telemetry data with additional resource metadata from Resource Explorer.

GetTelemetryEvaluationStatus.name: GetTelemetryEvaluationStatus
GetTelemetryEvaluationStatus.documentation: Returns the current onboarding status of the telemetry config feature, including the status of the feature and reason the feature failed to start or stop.

GetTelemetryEvaluationStatusForOrganizat.name: GetTelemetryEvaluationStatusForOrganization
GetTelemetryEvaluationStatusForOrganizat.documentation: This returns the onboarding status of the telemetry configuration feature for the organization. It can only be called by a Management Account of an Amazon Web Services Organization or an assigned Delegated Admin Account of Amazon CloudWatch telemetry config.

GetTelemetryPipeline.name: GetTelemetryPipeline
GetTelemetryPipeline.documentation: Retrieves information about a specific telemetry pipeline, including its configuration, status, and metadata.

GetTelemetryRule.name: GetTelemetryRule
GetTelemetryRule.documentation: Retrieves the details of a specific telemetry rule in your account.

GetTelemetryRuleForOrganization.name: GetTelemetryRuleForOrganization
GetTelemetryRuleForOrganization.documentation: Retrieves the details of a specific organization telemetry rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

GetThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment.name: GetThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment
GetThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment.documentation: Returns the details of a third-party telemetry enrichment, including its status and source configuration.

ListCentralizationRulesForOrganization.name: ListCentralizationRulesForOrganization
ListCentralizationRulesForOrganization.documentation: Lists all centralization rules in your organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

ListConnectors.name: ListConnectors
ListConnectors.documentation: Lists the connectors in the account and Region. This operation returns results in pages. To get the next page, pass the returned NextToken in the next call. We recommend that you use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.

ListDatasetIntegrations.name: ListDatasetIntegrations
ListDatasetIntegrations.documentation: Returns the dataset integrations in your account.

ListResourceTelemetry.name: ListResourceTelemetry
ListResourceTelemetry.documentation: Returns a list of telemetry configurations for Amazon Web Services resources supported by telemetry config. For more information, see Auditing CloudWatch telemetry configurations.

ListResourceTelemetryForOrganization.name: ListResourceTelemetryForOrganization
ListResourceTelemetryForOrganization.documentation: Returns a list of telemetry configurations for Amazon Web Services resources supported by telemetry config in the organization.

ListResourcesByConnector.name: ListResourcesByConnector
ListResourcesByConnector.documentation: Lists resources in your cloud provider that the connector can access, such as management groups, subscriptions, resource types, Regions, resources, and Event Hubs. Use the results to build a telemetry manifest. This operation returns results in pages. To get the next page, pass the returned NextToken in the next call. We recommend that you use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.

ListS3TableIntegrations.name: ListS3TableIntegrations
ListS3TableIntegrations.documentation: Lists all S3 Table integrations in your account. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.documentation: Lists all tags attached to the specified resource. Supports telemetry rule resources, telemetry pipeline resources, and third-party telemetry enrichment resources.

ListTelemetryPipelines.name: ListTelemetryPipelines
ListTelemetryPipelines.documentation: Returns a list of telemetry pipelines in your account. Returns up to 100 results. If more than 100 telemetry pipelines exist, include the NextToken value from the response to retrieve the next set of results.

ListTelemetryRules.name: ListTelemetryRules
ListTelemetryRules.documentation: Lists all telemetry rules in your account. You can filter the results by specifying a rule name prefix.

ListTelemetryRulesForOrganization.name: ListTelemetryRulesForOrganization
ListTelemetryRulesForOrganization.documentation: Lists all telemetry rules in your organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

ListThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichments.name: ListThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichments
ListThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichments.documentation: Returns a summary of each third-party telemetry enrichment in your account and Region. To get the full configuration of an enrichment, use GetThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment. The results are paginated. To get the next page of results, use NextToken.

PutConnectorTelemetryManifest.name: PutConnectorTelemetryManifest
PutConnectorTelemetryManifest.documentation: Creates or replaces the telemetry manifest of a connector. The telemetry manifest declares which resources in your cloud provider to collect telemetry from and which telemetry types to collect. To avoid overwriting changes made by another caller, specify ExpectedVersion.

StartTelemetryEnrichment.name: StartTelemetryEnrichment
StartTelemetryEnrichment.documentation: Enables the resource tags for telemetry feature for your account, which enhances telemetry data with additional resource metadata from Resource Explorer to provide richer context for monitoring and observability.

StartTelemetryEvaluation.name: StartTelemetryEvaluation
StartTelemetryEvaluation.documentation: This action begins onboarding the caller Amazon Web Services account to the telemetry config feature.

StartTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization.name: StartTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization
StartTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization.documentation: This actions begins onboarding the organization and all member accounts to the telemetry config feature.

StartTelemetryPipelineRefresh.name: StartTelemetryPipelineRefresh
StartTelemetryPipelineRefresh.documentation:
Starts a refresh of an external-cloud telemetry pipeline. The refresh re-reads the connector's telemetry manifest and re-discovers the sources in scope.

The pipeline must be in the ACTIVE or UPDATE_FAILED state, with no refresh already running. You can use GetTelemetryPipeline to track the refresh.

StartThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment.name: StartThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment
StartThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment.documentation:
Starts a third-party telemetry enrichment. An enrichment adds resource metadata, such as tags, from a third-party telemetry source to the telemetry that CloudWatch receives from the resources of that source.

You specify an Amazon Web Services Config connector for your third-party environment, such as a Microsoft Azure tenant. You can use each connector for only one enrichment.

To use this operation, you must have the config:PutThirdPartyServiceLinkedConfigurationRecorder permission. If the Amazon Web Services Config service-linked role does not exist in your account, you must also have the iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole permission.

StopTelemetryEnrichment.name: StopTelemetryEnrichment
StopTelemetryEnrichment.documentation: Disables the resource tags for telemetry feature for your account, stopping the enhancement of telemetry data with additional resource metadata.

StopTelemetryEvaluation.name: StopTelemetryEvaluation
StopTelemetryEvaluation.documentation: This action begins offboarding the caller Amazon Web Services account from the telemetry config feature.

StopTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization.name: StopTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization
StopTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization.documentation: This action offboards the Organization of the caller Amazon Web Services account from the telemetry config feature.

StopThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment.name: StopThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment
StopThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment.documentation:
Stops a third-party telemetry enrichment. CloudWatch stops adding resource metadata from the third-party telemetry source to your telemetry.

To use this operation, you must have the config:DeleteServiceLinkedConfigurationRecorder permission.

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.documentation: Adds or updates tags for a resource. Supports telemetry rule resources, telemetry pipeline resources, and third-party telemetry enrichment resources.

TestTelemetryPipeline.name: TestTelemetryPipeline
TestTelemetryPipeline.documentation: Tests a pipeline configuration with sample records to validate data processing before deployment. This operation helps ensure your pipeline configuration works as expected.

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.documentation: Removes tags from a resource. Supports telemetry rule resources, telemetry pipeline resources, and third-party telemetry enrichment resources.

UpdateCentralizationRuleForOrganization.name: UpdateCentralizationRuleForOrganization
UpdateCentralizationRuleForOrganization.documentation: Updates an existing centralization rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

UpdateDatasetIntegration.name: UpdateDatasetIntegration
UpdateDatasetIntegration.documentation: Updates a dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region. This operation is idempotent; if you submit the same update more than once, each call succeeds.

UpdateTelemetryPipeline.name: UpdateTelemetryPipeline
UpdateTelemetryPipeline.documentation:
Updates the configuration of an existing telemetry pipeline.

The following attributes cannot be updated after pipeline creation:

  • Pipeline name - The pipeline name is immutable

  • Pipeline ARN - The ARN is automatically generated and cannot be changed

  • Source type - Once a pipeline is created with a specific source type (such as S3, CloudWatch Logs, GitHub, or third-party sources), it cannot be changed to a different source type

Processors can be added, removed, or modified. However, some processors are not supported for third-party pipelines and cannot be added through updates.

Source-Specific Update Rules

CloudWatch Logs Sources (Vended and Custom)

Updatable: sts_role_arn

Fixed: data_source_name, data_source_type, sink (must remain @original)

S3 Sources (Crowdstrike, Zscaler, SentinelOne, Custom)

Updatable: All SQS configuration parameters, sts_role_arn, codec settings, compression type, bucket ownership settings, sink log group

Fixed: notification_type, aws.region

GitHub Audit Logs

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, scope (can switch between ORGANIZATION/ENTERPRISE), organization or enterprise name, range, authentication credentials (PAT or GitHub App)

Microsoft Sources (Entra ID, Office365, Windows)

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, tenant_id, workspace_id (Windows only), OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

Okta Sources (SSO, Auth0)

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, domain, range, OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

Palo Alto Networks

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, hostname, basic authentication credentials (username, password)

ServiceNow CMDB

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, instance_url, range, OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

Wiz CNAPP

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, region, range, OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

UpdateTelemetryRule.name: UpdateTelemetryRule
UpdateTelemetryRule.documentation: Updates an existing telemetry rule in your account. If multiple users attempt to modify the same telemetry rule simultaneously, a ConflictException is returned to provide specific error information for concurrent modification scenarios.

UpdateTelemetryRuleForOrganization.name: UpdateTelemetryRuleForOrganization
UpdateTelemetryRuleForOrganization.documentation: Updates an existing telemetry rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.

ValidateTelemetryPipelineConfiguration.name: ValidateTelemetryPipelineConfiguration
ValidateTelemetryPipelineConfiguration.documentation: Validates a pipeline configuration without creating the pipeline. This operation checks the configuration for syntax errors and compatibility issues.

AccessDeniedException.documentation: Indicates you don't have permissions to perform the requested operation. The user or role that is making the request must have at least one IAM permissions policy attached that grants the required permissions. For more information, see Access management for Amazon Web Services resources in the IAM user guide.

Action.documentation: Enumeration of WAF actions that can be matched in filter conditions.
The WAF action to match against (ALLOW, BLOCK, COUNT, CAPTCHA, CHALLENGE, EXCLUDED_AS_COUNT).

ActionCondition.documentation: Condition that matches based on the specific WAF action taken on the request.

Name.documentation: An optional, descriptive name for an advanced event selector, such as "Log data events for only two S3 buckets".

FieldSelectors.documentation: Contains all selector statements in an advanced event selector.

AdvancedEventSelector.documentation: Advanced event selectors let you create fine-grained selectors for management, data, and network activity events.

Field.documentation: The name of the field to use for selection.

Equals.documentation: Matches if the field value equals the specified value.

StartsWith.documentation: Matches if the field value starts with the specified value.

EndsWith.documentation: Matches if the field value ends with the specified value.

NotEquals.documentation: Matches if the field value does not equal the specified value.

NotStartsWith.documentation: Matches if the field value does not start with the specified value.

NotEndsWith.documentation: Matches if the field value does not end with the specified value.

AdvancedFieldSelector.documentation: Defines criteria for selecting resources based on field values.

AllSubscriptions.documentation: Selects every Azure subscription that Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) allows the connector to read. Subscriptions that the connector can read later are included automatically.

RetentionDays.documentation: The number of days that the created Storage Accounts keep Flow Logs.

AzureAwsManagedFlowLogs.documentation: Configuration for Flow Log Storage Accounts that the setup creates, one in each Region that ingests Flow Logs.

TenantIdentifier.documentation: The ID of the Microsoft Entra ID tenant.

ClientIdentifier.documentation: The application (client) ID of the Azure app registration. The app registration must have a federated identity credential that trusts the Amazon Web Services OpenID Connect (OIDC) issuer for your account.

AzureConnectorConfiguration.documentation: The configuration of a connector to Microsoft Azure.

ResourceTypes.documentation: Lists the Azure resource types that have resources in scope.

Regions.documentation: Lists the Azure Regions that have resources in scope.

AzureConnectorQuery.documentation: The type of Azure resource to list. Specify one type.

AzureConnectorQueryResults.documentation: The results of an Azure discovery query. The populated member matches the member of the query.

StorageAccounts.documentation: The Storage Accounts that store your Flow Logs, listed by Azure Region. Each Region can appear only once, and each Storage Account can appear only once across all Regions.

AzureCustomerManagedFlowLogs.documentation: Configuration for existing Azure Storage Accounts that already receive your Flow Logs.

PartitionCount.documentation: The number of partitions in each Event Hub. The Standard tier allows 1–32 partitions and the Premium tier allows 1–100. On the Standard tier, you can't change this value after the setup creates the Event Hub.

AzureEventHubConfiguration.documentation: Configuration of the Azure Event Hubs that the setup creates to deliver resource logs.

ResourceId.documentation: The Azure Resource Manager ID of the Event Hub.

NamespaceName.documentation: The name of the Event Hubs namespace that contains the Event Hub.

FullyQualifiedNamespace.documentation: The fully qualified host name of the Event Hubs namespace, for example <namespace>.servicebus.windows.net. The suffix differs in sovereign clouds.

Region.documentation: The Azure Region of the Event Hub, for example eastus.

SubscriptionId.documentation: The Azure subscription that contains the Event Hub.

Scope.documentation: Limits the query to a management group or to specific subscriptions.

NamespaceName.documentation: Limits the results to Event Hubs in this namespace.

Region.documentation: Limits the results to one Azure Region, for example eastus.

AzureEventHubsQuery.documentation: A query that lists Azure Event Hubs.

Region.documentation: The Azure Region of the Storage Accounts, for example eastus.

StorageAccountIds.documentation: The Azure Resource Manager IDs of the Storage Accounts.

AzureFlowLogStorageAccountScope.documentation: The Azure Storage Accounts in one Azure Region that store Flow Logs.

CustomerManaged.documentation: Use your existing Storage Accounts that already store Flow Logs.

AwsManaged.documentation: Create one Storage Account in each Azure Region that ingests Flow Logs, in the subscription specified by SubscriptionId.

AzureFlowLogsInfrastructure.documentation: The location of your Flow Logs: your existing Storage Accounts, or Storage Accounts that the setup creates. Specify one.

SubscriptionId.documentation: The Azure subscription in which the setup creates the Event Hubs namespaces and, for AwsManaged Flow Logs, the Storage Accounts. You must specify this value if an AzureScopeItem collects ResourceLogs, or if you specify EventHubs or AwsManaged Flow Logs.

EventHubs.documentation: The Event Hubs configuration. Specify exactly one entry, which applies to the Event Hubs in every Azure Region. This value applies only if an AzureScopeItem collects ResourceLogs. If you omit it, the setup uses default settings.

FlowLogs.documentation: The location of your Flow Logs. You must specify this value if an AzureScopeItem collects FlowLogs, and you can specify it only in that case.

AzureInfrastructure.documentation: The choices for the Azure infrastructure that the setup creates.

DisplayName.documentation: The display name of the management group.

ParentManagementGroupId.documentation: Lists the management groups under this management group. If you omit this value, the query starts at the tenant root group.

AzureManagementGroupsQuery.documentation: A query that lists Azure management groups.

ManagementGroupId.documentation: Limits the query to resources under this management group.

SubscriptionIds.documentation: Limits the query to these subscriptions. You can specify 1–1000 subscriptions.

AzureQueryScope.documentation: Limits a query to a management group or to specific subscriptions.

Scope.documentation: Limits the query to a management group or to specific subscriptions.

AzureRegionsQuery.documentation: A query that lists the Azure Regions that have resources in scope.

Region.documentation: The Azure Region of the resources, for example eastus. Required because an Azure resource ID doesn't include the Region.

ResourceIds.documentation: The Azure Resource Manager IDs of the resources.

ResourceId.documentation: The Azure Resource Manager ID of the resource.

Region.documentation: The Azure Region of the resource, for example eastus.

SubscriptionId.documentation: The Azure subscription that contains the resource.

Tags.documentation: The tags on the resource. Absent if the resource has no tags.

Scope.documentation: Limits the query to a management group or to specific subscriptions.

ResourceType.documentation: Limits the results to one Azure resource type, for example Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines.

Region.documentation: Limits the results to one Azure Region, for example eastus.

TagFilters.documentation: Limits the results to resources that have these tags. A resource must match the filters for all tag keys, and any of the values for each key. The service matches tag keys and values case-insensitively, as Azure does.

Scope.documentation: Limits the query to a management group or to specific subscriptions.

AzureResourceTypesQuery.documentation: A query that lists the Azure resource types that have resources in scope.

Subscriptions.documentation: The subscriptions to find resources in: all subscriptions that the connector can read, or a list of subscriptions. Required when you use Regions and ResourceTypes.

Regions.documentation: The Azure Regions to find resources in. Required when you use Subscriptions and ResourceTypes.

ResourceTypes.documentation: The Azure resource types to find. Required when you use Subscriptions and Regions.

TagFilters.documentation: Limits the resources found by Subscriptions, Regions, and ResourceTypes to those that have these tags. You can specify up to 50 filters.

Resources.documentation: Specific Azure resources, listed by Azure Region.

AzureScope.documentation:
The Azure resources to collect telemetry from. These are the resources found by Subscriptions, Regions, and ResourceTypes, optionally narrowed by TagFilters, plus any resources listed in Resources. You can specify:

  • Subscriptions, Regions, and ResourceTypes together

  • Resources

  • Both

Scope.documentation: The Azure resources to collect telemetry from.

AzureScopeItem.documentation: The telemetry types to collect from a set of Azure resources.

All.documentation: All subscriptions that Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) allows the connector to read. Subscriptions that the connector can read later are included automatically.

AzureSubscriptionScope.documentation: The subscriptions to find resources in: all subscriptions that the connector can read, or a list of subscriptions. Specify one.

State.documentation: The state of the subscription in Azure, for example Enabled.

ManagementGroupId.documentation: The ID of the management group that contains the subscription.
Limits the results to subscriptions under this management group.

AwsConfigConnectorArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Config connector for the Microsoft Azure tenant to collect resource metadata from.

AzureTelemetrySourceConfigurationInput.documentation: The Microsoft Azure source configuration for a third-party telemetry enrichment.

AwsConfigConnectorArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Config connector that the enrichment uses.

ServiceLinkedRecorderArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the service-linked configuration recorder that CloudWatch created in your account for the enrichment.

AzureTelemetrySourceConfigurationOutput.documentation: The Microsoft Azure source configuration of a third-party telemetry enrichment.

Source.documentation: Configuration determining the source of the telemetry data to be centralized.

Destination.documentation: Configuration determining where the telemetry data should be centralized, backed up, as well as encryption configuration for the primary and backup destinations.

CentralizationRule.documentation: Defines how telemetry data should be centralized across an Amazon Web Services Organization, including source and destination configurations.

Region.documentation: The primary destination region to which telemetry data should be centralized.

Account.documentation: The destination account (within the organization) to which the telemetry data should be centralized.

DestinationLogsConfiguration.documentation: Log specific configuration for centralization destination log groups.

DestinationMetricsConfiguration.documentation: Metric specific configuration for centralization destination metrics.

CentralizationRuleDestination.documentation: Configuration specifying the primary destination for centralized telemetry data.

Regions.documentation: The list of source regions from which telemetry data should be centralized.

Scope.documentation: The organizational scope from which telemetry data should be centralized, specified using organization id, accounts or organizational unit ids.

SourceLogsConfiguration.documentation: Log specific configuration for centralization source log groups.

SourceMetricsConfiguration.documentation: Metric specific configuration for centralization source metrics.

SourceContextGraphConfiguration.documentation: Configuration that enables centralization of the context graph for the selected sources. Including this configuration in a rule's source opts the rule into centralizing the context graph for the selected sources.

CentralizationRuleSource.documentation: Configuration specifying the source of telemetry data to be centralized.

RuleName.documentation: The name of the organization centralization rule.

RuleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the organization centralization rule.

CreatorAccountId.documentation: The Amazon Web Services Account that created the organization centralization rule.

CreatedTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the organization centralization rule was created.

CreatedRegion.documentation: The Amazon Web Services region where the organization centralization rule was created.

LastUpdateTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the organization centralization rule was last updated.

RuleHealth.documentation: The health status of the organization centralization rule.

FailureReason.documentation: The reason why an organization centralization rule is marked UNHEALTHY.

TagPropagationStatus.documentation: The health status of tag propagation for this rule. This status is independent of the overall RuleHealth for log delivery. Returns Healthy when the most recent tag-propagation attempt succeeded, or Unhealthy when the most recent attempt failed.

TagPropagationFailureReason.documentation: The reason tag propagation is unhealthy for this rule. Only present when TagPropagationStatus is Unhealthy.

ContextGraphStatus.documentation: The status of context graph centralization for this rule. Returns Provisioning while the context graph is being set up, Healthy once it is active, or Unhealthy if provisioning failed. This status is independent of the overall RuleHealth for log delivery.

DestinationAccountId.documentation: The primary destination account of the organization centralization rule.

DestinationRegion.documentation: The primary destination region of the organization centralization rule.

CentralizationRuleSummary.documentation: A summary of a centralization rule's key properties and status.

AdvancedEventSelectors.documentation: The advanced event selectors to use for filtering Amazon Web Services CloudTrail events.

CloudtrailParameters.documentation: Parameters specific to Amazon Web Services CloudTrail telemetry configuration.

ActionCondition.documentation: Matches log records based on the WAF rule action taken (ALLOW, BLOCK, COUNT, etc.).

LabelNameCondition.documentation: Matches log records based on WAF rule labels applied to the request.

Condition.documentation: A single condition that can match based on WAF rule action or label name.

Conditions.documentation: A list of conditions for filter matching, with at least one condition required.

Sources.documentation: The list of data sources configured in the pipeline.

DataSources.documentation: The list of data sources that provide telemetry data to the pipeline.

Processors.documentation: The list of processors configured in the pipeline for data transformation.

ProcessorCount.documentation: The total number of processors configured in the pipeline.

Sinks.documentation: The list of destinations where processed data is sent.

ConfigurationSummary.documentation: Provides a summary of pipeline configuration components including sources, processors, and destinations.

ResourceId.documentation: The identifier of the resource which is in conflict with the requested operation.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of the resource which is in conflict with the requested operation.

ConflictException.documentation: The requested operation conflicts with the current state of the specified resource or with another request.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the connector.

Provider.documentation: The cloud provider that the connector connects to.

ConnectorConfiguration.documentation: The configuration for connecting to the third-party cloud provider.

RoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that CloudWatch assumes to obtain credentials for the third-party cloud provider.

CreatedTimeStamp.documentation: The time when the connector was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

Connector.documentation: A connector to a third-party cloud provider.

Azure.documentation: The configuration of a connector to Microsoft Azure.

ConnectorConfiguration.documentation: The configuration for connecting to a third-party cloud provider. Specify one provider.

Azure.documentation: The type of Azure resource to list.

ConnectorQuery.documentation: What to list in a cloud provider. Specify one provider.

Azure.documentation: The results of an Azure discovery query.

ConnectorQueryResults.documentation: The results of a query. The populated member matches the member of the query.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the connector.

Provider.documentation: The cloud provider that the connector connects to.

CreatedTimeStamp.documentation: The time when the connector was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

ContextGraphStatus.documentation: The status of context graph centralization for a centralization rule. This status is independent of the overall RuleHealth for log delivery. Returns Provisioning while the context graph is being set up, Healthy once it is active, or Unhealthy if provisioning failed.

RuleName.documentation: A unique name for the organization-wide centralization rule being created.

Rule.documentation: The configuration details for the organization-wide centralization rule, including the source configuration and the destination configuration to centralize telemetry data across the organization.

Tags.documentation: The key-value pairs to associate with the organization telemetry rule resource for categorization and management purposes.

RuleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the created organization centralization rule.

ConnectorConfiguration.documentation: The configuration for connecting to the third-party cloud provider.

RoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that CloudWatch assumes to get credentials for the third-party cloud provider. The role must trust the Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin service principal, observabilityadmin.amazonaws.com. The role must also allow sts:GetWebIdentityToken for the provider's token exchange audience.

Name.documentation:
The name of the connector. The name must be unique in the account and Region (case-sensitive). If another connector already uses the name, the request fails with a ConflictException.

The name can contain letters, digits, hyphens (-), underscores (_) and periods (.), and must start with a letter.

Tags.documentation: The tags that you want to apply to the connector.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to ensure the operation completes no more than one time. If you use an Amazon Web Services SDK, the SDK generates this value and reuses it on retries. If this token matches a previous request with the same parameters, the service returns the connector from the first request without an error. Status.documentation: The status of the operation in this region. For telemetry evaluation, valid values include STARTING, RUNNING, and FAILED_START. For telemetry rules, valid values include PENDING, ACTIVE, and FAILED.

FailureReason.documentation: The reason for a failure status in this region. This field is only populated when Status indicates a failure.

RuleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry rule in this spoke region. This field is only present for telemetry rule region statuses and is populated when the rule has been successfully created in the spoke region (status is ACTIVE).

RegionStatus.documentation: Represents the status of a multi-region operation in a specific Amazon Web Services Region. This structure is used to report per-region progress for both telemetry evaluation and telemetry rule replication.

ResourceId.documentation: The identifier of the resource which could not be found.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of the resource which could not be found.

ResourceNotFoundException.documentation: The specified resource (such as a telemetry rule) could not be found.

ResourceId.documentation: The identifier of the resource which exceeds the service quota.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of the resource which exceeds the service quota.

ServiceCode.documentation: The code for the service of the exceeded quota.

QuotaCode.documentation: The code for the exceeded service quota.

ServiceQuotaExceededException.documentation: The requested operation would exceed the allowed quota for the specified resource type.

ContentType.documentation: The content type of the artifact, for example text/plain.

SetupArtifact.documentation: A setup artifact, which is one file in the requested format.

Name.documentation: The name value, limited to 64 characters.

SingleHeader.documentation: Structure containing a name field limited to 64 characters for header or query parameter identification.

Type.documentation: The plugin name of the source, such as cloudwatch_logs or s3.

Source.documentation: A list of source plugin types used in the pipeline configuration (such as cloudwatch_logs or s3). Currently supports a single source per pipeline, but is structured as a list to accommodate multiple pipelines in the configuration.

SourceContextGraphConfiguration.documentation: Configuration that enables centralization of the context graph for the selected sources. Including this configuration in a rule's source opts the rule into centralizing the context graph for the selected sources.

LogGroupSelectionCriteria.documentation: The selection criteria that specifies which source log groups to centralize. The selection criteria uses the same format as OAM link filters.

DataSourceSelectionCriteria.documentation: The selection criteria that specifies which data sources to centralize. The selection criteria uses the same filter expression format as LogGroupSelectionCriteria, but operates on DataSourceName and DataSourceType operands. When both LogGroupSelectionCriteria and DataSourceSelectionCriteria are specified, a log event must match both criteria to be centralized.

EncryptedLogGroupStrategy.documentation: A strategy determining whether to centralize source log groups that are encrypted with customer managed KMS keys (CMK). ALLOW will consider CMK encrypted source log groups for centralization while SKIP will skip CMK encrypted source log groups from centralization.

SourceLogsConfiguration.documentation: Configuration for selecting and handling source log groups for centralization.

MetricsSelectionCriteria.documentation: The filter expression that selects which source metrics to centralize. Currently, only * (all metrics) is supported. Other values return a validation error.

SourceMetricsConfiguration.documentation: Configuration for selecting source metrics for centralization.

ProfilesSelectionCriteria.documentation: The filter expression that selects which source profiles to centralize.

SourceProfilesConfiguration.documentation: Configuration for selecting source profiles for centralization.

Active.documentation: The number of discovered sources that are active and sending telemetry to the pipeline.

Total.documentation: The total number of sources discovered for the pipeline.

SourceProgress.documentation: A summary of source activation for an external-cloud telemetry pipeline, with the number of active sources and the total number of discovered sources.

Status.documentation: The status of the resource tags for telemetry feature after the start operation (Running, Stopped, or Impaired).

AwsResourceExplorerManagedViewArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Resource Explorer managed view created for resource tags for telemetry.

Regions.documentation: An optional list of Amazon Web Services Regions to include in multi-region telemetry evaluation for the organization. The current region is always implicitly included and must not be specified in this list. When provided, telemetry evaluation starts in the current region and propagates to all specified regions for the organization. Mutually exclusive with AllRegions. If neither Regions nor AllRegions is provided, the operation applies only to the current region.

AllRegions.documentation: If set to true, telemetry evaluation for the organization starts in all Amazon Web Services Regions where Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin is available in the current partition. The current region becomes the home region for managing multi-region evaluation for the organization. When new regions become available, evaluation automatically expands to include them. Mutually exclusive with Regions.

Regions.documentation: An optional list of Amazon Web Services Regions to include in multi-region telemetry evaluation. The current region is always implicitly included and must not be specified in this list. When provided, telemetry evaluation starts in the current region and propagates to all specified regions. Mutually exclusive with AllRegions. If neither Regions nor AllRegions is provided, the operation applies only to the current region.

AllRegions.documentation: If set to true, telemetry evaluation starts in all Amazon Web Services Regions where Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin is available in the current partition. The current region becomes the home region for managing multi-region evaluation. When new regions become available, evaluation automatically expands to include them. Mutually exclusive with Regions.

PipelineIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry pipeline to refresh.

Name.documentation: A name for the enrichment. The name must be unique in your account and Region. You can use the name instead of the ARN to identify the enrichment in other operations.

TelemetrySourceConfiguration.documentation: The third-party telemetry source to collect resource metadata from. Specify exactly one telemetry source.

Tags.documentation: The tags to associate with the enrichment resource.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the enrichment.

Status.documentation:
The status of the enrichment after the start operation. Valid values:

  • Initializing - CloudWatch is setting up the enrichment. Some telemetry can be enriched before setup completes.

  • Running - The enrichment is active.

  • Stopped - The enrichment is stopped.

  • Impaired - The enrichment has a problem. StatusReason describes the problem.

StatusReason.documentation: The reason for the current status. This field is present when the status is Impaired.

Status.documentation: The status of the resource tags for telemetry feature after the stop operation (Running, Stopped, or Impaired).

TelemetryEnrichmentIdentifier.documentation:
The identifier of the enrichment to stop. You can specify one of the following:

  • The name of the enrichment.

  • The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the enrichment.

TelemetrySource.documentation: The third-party telemetry source of the enrichment.

Status.documentation:
The status of the enrichment after the stop operation. Valid values:

  • Initializing - CloudWatch is setting up the enrichment. Some telemetry can be enriched before setup completes.

  • Running - The enrichment is active.

  • Stopped - The enrichment is stopped.

  • Impaired - The enrichment has a problem. StatusReason describes the problem.

StatusReason.documentation: The reason for the current status. This field is present when the status is Impaired.

TagConflictResolutionStrategy.documentation:
The strategy for resolving tag conflicts between source and destination log groups.

  • ADD_ONLY – Only adds new tags from the source without modifying existing destination tags.

  • UPDATE_SYNC – Adds new tags and updates existing tags from the source. Does not remove destination tags that are absent from the source.

  • IN_SYNC – Keeps destination tags fully synchronized with source tags, including removing destination tags that do not exist on the source.

Key.documentation: The tag key. Up to 512 characters. The characters < > % & \ ? / $ { } ' " ` and control characters aren't allowed.

Values.documentation: The tag values to match. A resource matches if it has any of these values for the tag key.

TagFilter.documentation: A tag filter. A resource matches only if it has the tag. Filters for different tag keys must all match; for one tag key, any of the values can match.

DestinationRoleArn.documentation: The ARN of a customer-managed IAM role in the destination account. The service assumes this role to propagate tags to destination log groups. You must have iam:PassRole permission on this role.

TagConflictResolutionStrategy.documentation:
The strategy for resolving conflicts when a tag key exists on both the source and destination log groups. If not specified, defaults to UPDATE_SYNC.

  • ADD_ONLY – Only adds new tags from the source without modifying existing destination tags.

  • UPDATE_SYNC – Adds new tags and updates existing tags from the source. Does not remove destination tags that are absent from the source.

  • IN_SYNC – Keeps destination tags fully synchronized with source tags, including removing destination tags that do not exist on the source.

TagPropagationConfiguration.documentation: Specifies configuration for propagating resource tags from source log groups to centralized destination log groups. The service uses a customer-managed IAM role in the destination account to add, update, and remove tags on destination log groups.

TagPropagationFailureReason.documentation:
The reason tag propagation is unhealthy for a centralization rule.

  • RoleNotAssumable – The service cannot assume the destination role due to a trust policy or external ID misconfiguration.

  • RoleLacksPermissions – The role was assumed successfully but the tag API call was denied by the role's permissions policy.

TagPropagationStatus.documentation: The health status of tag propagation for a centralization rule. This status is independent of the overall RuleHealth for log delivery.

ResourceARN.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry rule resource to tag.

Tags.documentation: The key-value pairs to add or update for the telemetry rule resource.

AccountIdentifier.documentation: The account ID which contains the resource managed in telemetry configuration. An example of a valid account ID is 012345678901.

TelemetryConfigurationState.documentation: The configuration state for the resource, for example { Logs: NotApplicable; Metrics: Enabled; Traces: NotApplicable; Insights: NotApplicable; }.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of resource, for example Amazon Web Services::EC2::Instance, or Amazon Web Services::EKS::Cluster, etc.

ResourceIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the resource, for example for Amazon VPC, it would be vpc-1a2b3c4d5e6f1a2b3.

ResourceTags.documentation: Tags associated with the resource, for example { Name: "ExampleInstance", Environment: "Development" }.

LastUpdateTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp of the last change to the telemetry configuration for the resource. For example, 1728679196318.

TelemetryConfiguration.documentation: A model representing the state of a resource within an account according to telemetry config.

DestinationType.documentation: The type of destination for the telemetry data (e.g., "Amazon CloudWatch Logs", "S3").

DestinationPattern.documentation: The pattern used to generate the destination path or name, supporting macros like <resourceId> and <accountId>.

RetentionInDays.documentation: The number of days to retain the telemetry data in the destination.

VPCFlowLogParameters.documentation: Configuration parameters specific to VPC Flow Logs when VPC is the resource type.

CloudtrailParameters.documentation: Configuration parameters specific to Amazon Web Services CloudTrail when CloudTrail is the source type.

ELBLoadBalancerLoggingParameters.documentation: Configuration parameters specific to ELB load balancer logging when ELB is the resource type.

WAFLoggingParameters.documentation: Configuration parameters specific to WAF logging when WAF is the resource type.

LogDeliveryParameters.documentation: The configuration parameters for log delivery when the resource type supports configurable log types, such as Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment managers, or Elastic Load Balancing Application Load Balancers.

MskMonitoringParameters.documentation: Configuration parameters specific to MSK monitoring when MSK is the resource type.

KmsKeyArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer-managed Amazon Web Services KMS key used to encrypt the log groups created during telemetry rule remediation.

TelemetryDestinationConfiguration.documentation: Configuration specifying where and how telemetry data should be delivered for Amazon Web Services resources.

Source.documentation: The resources to collect telemetry from and the telemetry types to collect.

Infrastructure.documentation: The choices for the infrastructure that the setup creates in your cloud provider, such as the subscription that contains the Event Hubs and their size. If you omit this value, the setup uses default settings. If an AzureScopeItem collects ResourceLogs, you must specify at least the Azure SubscriptionId.

TelemetryManifest.documentation: Declares which resources in a cloud provider to collect telemetry from and which telemetry types to collect.

Azure.documentation: The choices for the Azure infrastructure that the setup creates.

TelemetryManifestInfrastructure.documentation: The choices for the infrastructure that the setup creates. Specify one provider, which must match the provider in Source.

Azure.documentation: The Azure scope items. Each AzureScopeItem specifies a set of Azure resources and the telemetry types to collect from them. You can specify up to 100 scope items.

TelemetryManifestSource.documentation: The resources to collect telemetry from, for one cloud provider. Specify one provider.

CreatedTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the telemetry pipeline was created.

LastUpdateTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the telemetry pipeline was last updated.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry pipeline.

Configuration.documentation: The configuration that defines how the telemetry pipeline processes data.

Status.documentation: The current status of the telemetry pipeline.

StatusReason.documentation: Additional information about the pipeline status, including reasons for failure states.

Tags.documentation: The key-value pairs associated with the telemetry pipeline resource.

LastRefreshTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the most recent refresh of the telemetry pipeline started. This field is only present for external-cloud pipelines that you have refreshed.

SourceProgress.documentation: The progress of source activation for the telemetry pipeline. This field is only present for external-cloud pipelines.

ConfigurationSummary.documentation: A summary of the pipeline configuration components.

TelemetryPipeline.documentation: Represents a complete telemetry pipeline resource with configuration, status, and metadata for data processing and transformation.

Body.documentation: The pipeline configuration body that defines the data processing rules and transformations.

TelemetryPipelineConfiguration.documentation:
Defines the configuration for a pipeline, including how data flows from sources through processors to destinations. The configuration is specified in YAML format and must include a valid pipeline definition with required source and sink components. This pipeline enables end-to-end telemetry data collection, transformation, and delivery while supporting optional processing steps and extensions for enhanced functionality.

The primary pipeline configuration section are:

  • Source: Defines where log data originates from (S3 buckets, CloudWatch Logs, third-party APIs). Each pipeline must have exactly one source.

  • Processors (optional): Transform, parse, and enrich log data as it flows through the pipeline. Processors are applied sequentially in the order they are defined.

  • Sink: Defines the destination where processed log data is sent. Each pipeline must have exactly one sink.

  • Extensions (optional): Provide additional functionality such as Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager integration for credential management.

For more details on each configuration section see CloudWatch pipelines User Guide. Additional comprehensive configuration examples can be found in the CreateTelemetryPipeline API docs.

Description.documentation: A description of the pipeline status reason, providing additional context about the current state.

TelemetryPipelineStatusReason.documentation: Provides detailed information about the status of a telemetry pipeline, including reasons for specific states.

CreatedTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the telemetry pipeline was created.

LastUpdateTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the telemetry pipeline was last updated.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry pipeline.

Status.documentation: The current status of the telemetry pipeline.

Tags.documentation: The key-value pairs associated with the telemetry pipeline resource.

ConfigurationSummary.documentation: A summary of the pipeline configuration components.

TelemetryPipelineSummary.documentation: Contains summary information about a telemetry pipeline for listing operations.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of Amazon Web Services resource to configure telemetry for (for example, AWS::EC2::VPC, AWS::EKS::Cluster, AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer, AWS::Bedrock::KnowledgeBase, AWS::BedrockAgentCore::PaymentManager, or AWS::XRay::TransactionSearchConfig).

TelemetryType.documentation: The type of telemetry to collect (Logs, Metrics, Traces, or Insights).

TelemetrySourceTypes.documentation: The specific telemetry source types to configure for the resource, such as VPC_FLOW_LOGS or EKS_AUDIT_LOGS. TelemetrySourceTypes must be correlated with the specific resource type.

DestinationConfiguration.documentation: Configuration specifying where and how the telemetry data should be delivered.

Scope.documentation: The organizational scope to which the rule applies, specified using accounts or organizational units.

SelectionCriteria.documentation: Criteria for selecting which resources the rule applies to, such as resource tags.

AllowFieldUpdates.documentation: If set to true, Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin detects and remediates configuration drift in telemetry resources that it manages. For example, if a VPC flow log's format, traffic type, or aggregation interval no longer matches the rule's destination configuration, the flow log is replaced with one that matches. Only Observability Admin-managed resources are updated; customer-created resources are never modified. Currently supported for AWS::EC2::VPC resources (VPC flow logs).

Regions.documentation: An optional list of Amazon Web Services Regions where this telemetry rule should be replicated. When specified, the rule is created in the home region and automatically replicated to all listed regions. Mutually exclusive with AllRegions.

AllRegions.documentation: If set to true, the telemetry rule is replicated to all Amazon Web Services Regions where Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin is available in the current partition. When new regions become available, the rule automatically replicates to them. Mutually exclusive with Regions.

TelemetryRule.documentation: Defines how telemetry should be configured for specific Amazon Web Services resources.

RuleName.documentation: The name of the telemetry rule.

RuleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry rule.

CreatedTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the telemetry rule was created.

LastUpdateTimeStamp.documentation: The timestamp when the telemetry rule was last modified.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of Amazon Web Services resource the rule applies to.

TelemetryType.documentation: The type of telemetry (Logs, Metrics, Traces, or Insights) the rule configures.

TelemetrySourceTypes.documentation: The types of telemetry sources configured for this rule, such as VPC Flow Logs or EKS audit logs. TelemetrySourceTypes must be correlated with the specific resource type.

TelemetryRuleSummary.documentation: A summary of a telemetry rule's key properties.

Azure.documentation: The configuration for a Microsoft Azure source.

TelemetrySourceConfigurationInput.documentation: The configuration of the third-party telemetry source that a new enrichment collects resource metadata from. Specify exactly one member.

Azure.documentation: The configuration of the Microsoft Azure source.

TelemetrySourceConfigurationOutput.documentation: The third-party source configuration of an enrichment.

TelemetrySourceType.documentation: Specifies the type of telemetry source for a resource, such as EKS cluster logs.

TelemetrySourceTypes.documentation: A list of telemetry source types that specify what kind of telemetry data to collect from a resource.

Records.documentation: The sample records to process through the pipeline configuration for testing purposes.

Configuration.documentation: The pipeline configuration to test with the provided sample records.

SignalType.documentation: The type of telemetry signal to test. If not specified, defaults to log processing.

Results.documentation: The results of processing the test records through the pipeline configuration, including any outputs or errors.

ThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichmentStatus.documentation: The status of a third-party telemetry enrichment.

TelemetrySource.documentation: The third-party telemetry source of the enrichment.

Status.documentation:
The current status of the enrichment. Valid values:

  • Initializing - CloudWatch is setting up the enrichment. Some telemetry can be enriched before setup completes.

  • Running - The enrichment is active.

  • Stopped - The enrichment is stopped.

  • Impaired - The enrichment has a problem. StatusReason describes the problem.

ThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichmentSummary.documentation: Summary information about a third-party telemetry enrichment, as returned by ListThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichments.

ThirdPartyTelemetrySource.documentation: A third-party telemetry source that can provide resource metadata.

TooManyRequestsException.documentation: The request throughput limit was exceeded.

ResourceARN.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the telemetry rule resource to remove tags from.

TagKeys.documentation: The list of tag keys to remove from the telemetry rule resource.

RuleIdentifier.documentation: The identifier (name or ARN) of the organization centralization rule to update.

Rule.documentation: The configuration details for the organization-wide centralization rule, including the source configuration and the destination configuration to centralize telemetry data across the organization.

RuleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the updated organization centralization rule.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the dataset integration to update.

RoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role to associate with the dataset integration.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the updated dataset integration.

RoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role associated with the updated dataset integration.

UpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the dataset integration was last updated.

Rule.documentation: The new configuration details for the organization telemetry rule, including resource type, telemetry type, and destination configuration.

RuleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the updated organization telemetry rule.

RedactedFields.documentation: The fields to redact from WAF logs to protect sensitive information.

LoggingFilter.documentation: A filter configuration that determines which WAF log records to include or exclude.

documentation:
You can use Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin to discover and understand the state of telemetry configuration in CloudWatch for your Amazon Web Services Organization or account. This simplifies the process of auditing your telemetry collection configurations across multiple resource types within your Amazon Web Services Organization or account. By providing a consolidated view, it allows you to easily review and manage telemetry settings, helping you ensure proper monitoring and data collection across your Amazon Web Services environment. For more information, see Auditing CloudWatch telemetry conﬁgurations in the CloudWatch User Guide.

For information on the permissions you need to use this API, see Identity and access management for Amazon CloudWatch in the CloudWatch User Guide.
